fields.name: paragraph
fields.label: Paragraph
fields.default: Your relationship with money isn't about maths. It's about the patterns you learnt long before you had a salary. The eight money types, developed by Deborah Price of the Money Coaching Institute, give those patterns names. Most people carry three or four, with one or two in charge, and they shift as life does.

fields.name: paragraph_2
fields.label: Paragraph 2
fields.default: Below, each type as I see it in the coaching room. Read them, notice which ones sting, then take the quiz.

fields.name: paragraph
fields.label: Paragraph
fields.default: Money feels big, confusing and slightly frightening, so the Innocent looks away and hopes it sorts itself out. Bills stay unopened, statements unread. They'd much rather someone they trust handled it. Underneath is not laziness but anxiety: looking means finding out.

fields.name: text_3
fields.label: Text 3
fields.default: In the coaching room: "I know I should check. I just… don't."

fields.name: paragraph_2
fields.label: Paragraph 2
fields.default: Money happens *to* the Victim. The economy, the landlord, the ex, the boss: there's always someone or something to blame, and often a real wound behind it. The pattern is waiting to be rescued rather than acting, which keeps the story true.

fields.name: text_6
fields.label: Text 6
fields.default: In the coaching room: "What's the point, it never works out for people like me."

fields.name: paragraph_3
fields.label: Paragraph 3
fields.default: Confident, disciplined, goal-driven. The Warrior sets a target, makes a plan, and uses both logic and gut to get there. This is the type most of us want more of. Its shadow is impatience with people who don't think the same way, including partners.

fields.name: text_9
fields.label: Text 9
fields.default: In the coaching room: "Just tell me the numbers and I'll do it."

fields.name: paragraph_4
fields.label: Paragraph 4
fields.default: Generous to a fault. The Martyr pays for everyone, lends to anyone, and puts their own future last. Often there's a quiet expectation that it will be repaid, in money or gratitude, and quiet resentment when it isn't. Very common among parents and eldest siblings.

fields.name: text_12
fields.label: Text 12
fields.default: In the coaching room: "I can't say no to my family."

fields.name: paragraph_5
fields.label: Paragraph 5
fields.default: The Fool loves the thrill: the splurge, the hot tip, the crypto at 2am. Optimistic and lucky, money comes easily and leaves just as fast, because the pull of now beats the plan for later. Fun at dinner, dangerous in a bull market.

fields.name: text_15
fields.label: Text 15
fields.default: In the coaching room: "I'll make it back next month."

fields.name: paragraph_6
fields.label: Paragraph 6
fields.default: The Creator wants freedom, meaning and time, and suspects money is a bit grubby. So they under-charge, avoid the business side, and quietly block the wealth that would actually buy the freedom they want. The work is making peace with being paid well for good work.

fields.name: text_18
fields.label: Text 18
fields.default: In the coaching room: "I didn't get into this for the money."

fields.name: paragraph_7
fields.label: Paragraph 7
fields.default: A Warrior who went too far. The Tyrant uses money to control: the partner, the children, the staff. Every euro is tracked, every purchase questioned. It looks like strength, but it's fear of losing control, and it costs relationships long before it costs money.

fields.name: text_21
fields.label: Text 21
fields.default: In the coaching room: usually it's the partner who books the session.

fields.name: paragraph_8
fields.label: Paragraph 8
fields.default: The Magician knows their money story, where the patterns came from, and chooses differently. Decisions line up with values. Money is a tool, not a threat. There's security without obsession, generosity without martyrdom, ambition without tyranny. Nobody is born one. Everyone can become one.

fields.name: text_24
fields.label: Text 24
fields.default: In the coaching room: this is where we're heading.
